name: Matronae

attributes.attribute: the Latin name of the Deae Matres, the Divine Mothers of the Continental Celts
usually shown as three seated figures of maiden, mother, and crone
goddesses of abundance and of the fertility of the land
cult held firm in the Rhineland under the byname Aufaniae
the plural of a river-god name that becomes the Marne
triadic images with cornucopia and a bare-breasted mother
the domestic Mothers named in Roman-British dedications

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Matronae is the Latin plural name of a group of mother goddesses. Koch counts 84 instances of the name in Roman-period dedications. The cult stood firm in the Rhineland, near Bonn and Cologne. There the goddesses carried the byname Aufaniae. Another shrine at Pesch kept the name Vacallinehae. The singular Matrona is also the old name of the Marne river. So one figure holds the name of a stream and its divine woman at once. The cult grew strongest around the Marne and spread west toward Britain. On later inscriptions the Mothers appear as a triad. They hold cornucopia, fruit, and other signs of plenty. They often nurse a baby with one breast bared. In Roman Britain the home goddesses, the Domesticae, gained dedications at York and at forts on the northern wall. The great count of images and shrines shows how central these mothers were.

okr.objective: Document the Matronae mother goddesses and their spread from the Marne to Britain.
